questions.text: Among simple LR (SLR) , canonical LR, and look-ahead LR (LALR), which of the following pairs identify the method that is very easy to implement and the method that is the most powerful , in that order?
questions.solution:
SLR uses LR(0) items with FOLLOW sets, so it is the simplest. Canonical LR(1) has the most states and recognises the largest class of grammars (most powerful). LALR lies in between.

Answer: SLR, canonical LR

questions.text:
Consider the intermediate code given below.
(1) i = 1
(2) j = 1
(3) t1 = 5 * i
(4) t2 = t1 + j
(5) t3 = 4 * t2
(6) t4 = t3
(7) a[t4] = -1
(8) j = j + 1
(9) if j[latex]\leq [/latex]5 goto (3)
(10) i=i+1
(11) if i[latex]\lt [/latex]5 goto (2)
The number of nodes and edges in the control-flow-graph constructed for the above code, respectively, are
questions.solution:
Leaders: (1), (2) (target of 11), (3) (target of 9), (10) (after a jump).
Blocks: B1 = {1}, B2 = {2}, B3 = {3-9}, B4 = {10, 11}, plus Entry and Exit [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 6 nodes.

Edges: Entry[latex]\rightarrow[/latex]B1, B1[latex]\rightarrow[/latex]B2, B2[latex]\rightarrow[/latex]B3, B3[latex]\rightarrow[/latex]B3, B3[latex]\rightarrow[/latex]B4, B4[latex]\rightarrow[/latex]B2, B4[latex]\rightarrow[/latex]Exit [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 7 edges.

Answer: 6 and 7

questions.text: In the context of abstract-syntax-tree (AST) and control-flow-graph (CFG), which one of the following is TRUE?
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- Option 1: in a CFG a loop edge goes back to earlier code [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] false.
- Option 2: CFGs have cycles for loops [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] false.
- Option 3: an AST node can have as many children as the construct needs, and a CFG node (e.g. switch) as many successors as the code has [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] True.
- Option 4: a CFG basic block can contain many statements [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] false.

Answer: The maximum number of successors depends on the input program

options: In both AST and CFG, let node N2 be the successor of node N1. In the input program, the code corresponding to N2 is present after the code corresponding to N1
For any input program, neither AST nor CFG will contain a cycle
The maximum number of successors of a node in an AST and a CFG depends on the input program
Each node in AST and CFG corresponds to at most one statement in the input program

questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- Lexical analysis: DFA minimization (2)
- Parsing: production (parse) tree (4)
- Register allocation: graph coloring (1)
- Expression evaluation: post-order traversal (3)

Answer: P-2, Q-4, R-1, S-3

questions.text: The least number of temporary variables required to create a three-address code in static single assignment form for the expression q + r / 3 + s - t * 5 + u * v /w is _______________.
questions.solution:
In SSA every result gets a new variable. Count the operations:

t1 = r / 3, t2 = q + t1, t3 = t2 + s, t4 = t * 5, t5 = t3 [latex]-[/latex] t4, t6 = u * v, t7 = t6 / w, t8 = t5 + t7

8 operations [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 8 temporaries

Answer: 8
